title: Calculus Readiness and Function Synthesis
description: A graph is positive, decreasing, concave upward, has domain all reals, and approaches y=2 as x grows. Name plausible families and identify one additional feature needed.
outcomes: Classify unfamiliar formulas, graphs, tables, and contexts using structural evidence.
Select and compare function models using patterns, residuals, domains, and parameter meanings.
Compare average rates across function families and interpret units and interval dependence.
Construct and simplify [f(x+h)-f(x)]/h and interpret its components.
Interpret tangent slope as a limiting value of secant slopes.
Recognize when a smooth graph appears linear under magnification and identify failures of local linearity.
Estimate limits from tables, graphs, and algebra while distinguishing approached value from function value.
Classify removable, jump, infinite, and endpoint discontinuities using function values and limiting behavior.
Synthesize finite and infinite input behavior across polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric families.
Use bracketing, iteration, finite differences, and residuals while evaluating sensitivity to rounding and parameter error.
Connect rates, rectangles, finite sums, net change, and area under a rate graph.
Analyze an unfamiliar multirepresentation problem by selecting and combining methods from the entire course.
sources: Lippman & Rasmussen, rates of change and function behavior
BetterGrades Calculus Limits and Continuity course
Stitz & Zeager, function synthesis and numerical methods
